messages.author: d54aba6af40f8c5e
messages.subject: Linear combination of predicted outcomes
parts:
I am examining:

(1) the predicted outcomes of a dataset (for individuals 1:n) 

and wish to compare to predicted outcomes to 

(2) a modified version of the data with an altered covariate across the same individuals.

I which to compare predicted outcomes (original versus modified) and find the probability that the original outcomes are higher the the ones from the modified dataset.

Below is an example using the random walk example provided in INLA documentation. Here I want a (non-sampling) way of computing Pr(y.hat > y.hat.preds).

Any help would be appreciated.

Thanks,

John

-------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(INLA)

rm(list=ls())
set.seed(1)

n <- 100
z <- seq(0,6,length.out=n)
y <- sin(z)+rnorm(n,mean=0,sd=0.5)
dat <- tibble(
    y=y,
    z=z
)

preds <- dat %>%
    mutate(
        y = NA,
        z=z+1
    )
dat.preds <- bind_rows(dat,preds)

f <- y ~ 1 +
    f(z,
      model="rw2",
      constr=TRUE,
      scale.model=TRUE
      ##hyper=list(theta = list(prior="pc.prec",param=c(1,0.01)))
      )

mod <- inla(
    f,
    data=dat.preds,
    family="gaussian",
    control.predictor=list(link=1, compute=TRUE)
)

N <- nrow(dat)
y.hat <- mod$summary.fitted.values[1:N,"mean"]
y.hat.preds <- mod$summary.fitted.values[N + 1:N,"mean"]

diff <- y.hat - y.hat.preds

Pr(diff > 0)???

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Linear combination of predicted outcomes
parts:
### since fitted values is a monotone mapping of the linear predictor, then
### y.hat > y.hat.preds < == > lin.hat > lin.preds.hat
### or the other way around if the link is decreasing

### that mean you can use the linear combinations for the difference and then
check these ones

M <- matrix(0, N, 2*N)
for(i in 1:N) {
M[i, i] <- 1
M[i, i + N] <- -1
}
lc <- inla.make.lincombs(Predictor = M)

control.predictor=list(link=1, compute=TRUE),
lincomb = lc
)
for(i in 1:N) {
## to make a quick approximation
m <- mod$summary.lincomb.derived[i, "mean"]
s <- mod$summary.lincomb.derived[i, "sd"]

print(c(i,
1-inla.pmarginal(0, mod$marginals.lincomb.derived[[i]]),
1-pnorm(0, mean = m, sd = s)))

}
